nodes.label: ARGUS — Os 1000 Olhos (permanent orchestrator)
nodes.rationale: ARGUS is defined explicitly as not a router but a permanent presence: it observes every decision, line of code, data flow, and user interaction before it is considered valid. When collective attention is needed it convenes a team (not a queue) because 'uma fila executa, uma equipe pensa'. It only returns to arbitrate on genuine impasses; otherwise it observes and facilitates, leaving the output owned by the team.

nodes.label: Protocolo I — Vigilância Permanente
nodes.rationale: ARGUS always answers four questions before convening any team: what is being asked, what already exists in the system, who has jurisdiction, and whether there are unsolicited risk signals — because an output that ignores invisible context is treated as a risk, not an output.

nodes.label: Protocolo II — Convocação (team summoning by context)
nodes.rationale: ARGUS convenes whole teams, not individual seeds, mapping context type (algorithm, interface, auth, architecture, privacy, etc.) to the team with jurisdiction, so that deliberation always starts from the right collective.
nodes.norm_label: protocolo ii — convocacao (team summoning by context)

nodes.label: Protocolo III — Deliberação (round-table participation forms)
nodes.rationale: The table has no head; every convened seed has equal voice and may CONCORDA, COMPLEMENTA, TENSIONA, CEDE, ESCALA, or ABSTÉM. No seed may silence another, speak for another's domain uninvited, or declare convergence alone, and no output is emitted while a tension remains unresolved.

nodes.label: Protocolo IV — Convergência (collective sign-off and archiving)
nodes.rationale: Deliberation converges only when every active seed has spoken, answered directed tensions, and reached a position; the output is then built collectively, each seed signing the part of its own domain — not assembled by a pipeline or hierarchy.
nodes.norm_label: protocolo iv — convergencia (collective sign-off and archiving)

nodes.label: Protocolo V — Impasse (arbitration hierarchy)
nodes.rationale: ARGUS arbitrates only on genuine impasse — two or more seeds in active tension that cannot converge — applying a fixed 20-item hierarchy of resolution; the highest-ranked seed prevails only on the specific conflicting point, and the rest of the deliberation stays collective.

nodes.label: Protocolo VI — Assinatura (mandatory collective signature)
nodes.rationale: No output is valid without the collective signature of active seeds; signing is distributed responsibility, declaring the output respects that seed's domain, and a seed unable to sign without violating its kernel_logic must flag it before convergence, not after.

nodes.label: Protocolo VII — Vocabulário Proibido Global (banned terms)
nodes.rationale: A fixed list of terms (hack, workaround, ad-hoc, quick-fix, zero bugs, confiança implícita, etc.) is banned from any seed output in any context; a single banned word invalidates the whole output and the responsible seed must redo its contribution before reconvergence.
nodes.norm_label: protocolo vii — vocabulario proibido global (banned terms)

nodes.label: 20-item hierarchy of resolution for arbitrated impasses
nodes.rationale: Ordered precedence used only for the specific conflicting point: formal logical correctness (Literate) > structural security (Sentinel) > data/identity protection (Sovereign) > artifact integrity (Scribe) > testability/quality (Scout) > architectural sustainability (Flux) > continuous compliance (BAU) > lifecycle/temporality (Herald) > surface minimization (Blast) > human factor/attack (Ghost) > findability/IA (PolarBear) > cognitive ergonomics (Compass) > empirical usability (Empiricus) > visual identity/accessibility (Canvas) > design-system consistency (Forge) > content clarity/voice (Quill) > risk coverage (Pareto) > exploratory investigation (Probe) > automation architecture (Scaffold) > resources/recurrence (RiverRaid).
nodes.norm_label: 20-item hierarchy of resolution for arbitrated impasses

nodes.label: Fase de arquivamento (post-convergence XDRS archiving phase)
nodes.rationale: After content-seed convergence, SCRIBE identifies type/subject/canonical path and structures frontmatter, HERALD evaluates impact and sets valid-from, SCRIBE then runs lint, updates the canonical index, and delivers a draft to a human for final validation. SCRIBE and HERALD do not participate in content deliberation, only in persistence, and are skipped entirely when the output will not be archived as an XDRS policy.
nodes.norm_label: fase de arquivamento (post-convergence xdrs archiving phase)

nodes.label: Decision: scoped + typed + subject folder structure for XDRS
nodes.rationale: A standard Decision Record mixes reason, rule, plan, how-to and topic view in one document; XDRS separates these into Policies (source of truth), Research (evidence), Plans (implementation), Skills (procedure) and Articles (overview) because this scales across scopes, stays navigable, and keeps files small and focused for AI agents.
nodes.norm_label: decision: scoped + typed + subject folder structure for xdrs

nodes.label: _local scope (workspace-local, non-shared, lowest precedence override)
nodes.rationale: _local is reserved for XDRS elements created locally to a project; it must never be shared or propagated, must always sit last in the root index so it overrides/extends other scopes, and is never linked from shared root indexes even though tools should still try it by default.

nodes.label: .filedist.lock external XDRs tracking mechanism
nodes.rationale: A file whose path appears in the workspace root .filedist.lock was distributed from an external source repository and must never be modified locally; changes go to the source repo and are re-extracted. Lint tools skip external scopes by default, and version-field diffs across .filedist.lock entries reveal what changed on upgrade.

nodes.label: Decision: structured policies with mandatory template, applicability metadata, and conflict rules
nodes.rationale: Policies must be the authoritative, concise, template-compliant source of truth with clear applicability metadata (apply-to, valid-from) so humans and agents can reliably decide whether and how a decision applies, and so within-scope conflicts must be resolved rather than left standing.
nodes.norm_label: decision: structured policies with mandatory template, applicability metadata, and conflict rules

nodes.label: Decision: agentskills-compatible skill packages co-located with XDRS
nodes.rationale: Chosen over a top-level skills/ directory decoupled from XDRS because co-location reuses proven agentskills tooling, aligns with the existing scope/subject hierarchy, and keeps skills close to the decisions they implement; skills sit on an automation gradient from human-only to agent-only execution.
nodes.norm_label: decision: agentskills-compatible skill packages co-located with xdrs

nodes.label: Decision: subject-level synthetic articles co-located with Policies
nodes.rationale: Chosen over a separate documentation repository because co-located articles are easier to discover, consistent with skill placement, and clearly distinct from the policies themselves, reducing drift risk versus a decoupled docs repo.
nodes.norm_label: decision: subject-level synthetic articles co-located with policies

nodes.label: Decision: semantic versioning aligned with decision impact (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH)
nodes.rationale: Package version must communicate expected upgrade impact so consumers can trust that patch upgrades are low risk, minor upgrades are additive, and major upgrades may require migration; the highest-impact change in a release defines the bump, and uncertainty should favor the more explicit bump.
nodes.norm_label: decision: semantic versioning aligned with decision impact (major.minor.patch)

nodes.label: Decision: IMRAD-based subject-level research documents co-located with XDRS
nodes.rationale: Chosen over inline long-form analysis inside the Policy because it preserves lifecycle context, keeps the Policy concise, gives readers a predictable structure, and raises evidence quality without demanding full academic statistical rigor.
nodes.norm_label: decision: imrad-based subject-level research documents co-located with xdrs

nodes.label: Decision: subject-level ephemeral plan documents co-located with Policies
nodes.rationale: Chosen over inline planning inside Policies because plans are ephemeral execution documents (deleted after implementation) while Policies are lasting decisions; mixing them would bloat Policies and blur what to delete after execution.
nodes.norm_label: decision: subject-level ephemeral plan documents co-located with policies

nodes.label: Decision: numbered rule blocks inside Details with canonical dot-notation citation syntax
nodes.rationale: Chosen over free-form prose rules with heading anchors because anchors are fragile across editors/renderers and break silently on rewording; stable two-digit rule numbers (never reused) plus policy-name.NN-title citations give a minimal, stable, tooling-compatible extension to the base Policy template.
nodes.norm_label: decision: numbered rule blocks inside details with canonical dot-notation citation syntax

nodes.label: Decision: Marp Markdown slides co-located in .assets/ next to the parent document
nodes.rationale: Slides must never exist as standalone artifacts without a parent decision; bidirectional links, strict naming (-slides suffix), and .assets/ placement keep presentations traceable to and consistent with the source document instead of drifting from it.
nodes.norm_label: decision: marp markdown slides co-located in .assets/ next to the parent document

nodes.label: EDR: Deployment Strategy (Push-to-Main Auto-Deploy)
nodes.rationale: EAI? requires frequent iteration with minimal manual intervention. Decision: push to main triggers Cloud Build which deploys automatically to Cloud Run (eai-producao); staging branch pushes deploy to eai-staging. Rollback is done by reverting the commit and pushing to main. Both environments share the same codebase, differing only via environment variables injected at runtime.

nodes.label: EDR: LGPD Anonymization
nodes.rationale: EAI? processes sensitive personal legal data (names, CPF, contracts, medical/employment data) submitted by users. Under LGPD, all user-submitted case data must be anonymized (via anonymizer.ts) before persisting to Firestore; raw text must never be stored. Gemini calls during simulation use original non-anonymized text but are transient. Secondary writes (save, history, stats) are isolated in independent try-catch blocks so a failure never blocks the user from seeing their result.

nodes.label: EDR: Judge Area Binding (INSTRUCAO VINCULANTE)
nodes.rationale: Mandatory INSTRUCAO VINCULANTE prefix binds judge and lawyer to session's legal area (defense-in-depth; see EDR-007 for primary fix).

nodes.label: EDR: Dynamic Legal Areas
nodes.rationale: All legal areas supported via dynamic agent creation and Firestore caching.

nodes.label: EDR: Judge Impartiality in Creation
nodes.rationale: Judge and desembargadora descriptions to Shaw must always be impartial — userSide must never influence judge creation.

nodes.label: EDR: Demand-Driven Agent Creation
nodes.rationale: Agents are created exclusively on demand inside resolveAgent's Camada 3; registry curation is strictly subtractive/relocational and must never trigger compensatory agent creation.

nodes.label: EDR: Modo 1 Input Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Every limit shown in the Modo 1/2 input step's copy (attachments, minimum causa length) must be enforced in code, reusing the pattern already validated in lexforum-app.

nodes.label: EDR: SpecificJudge Null Sentinel Filtering
nodes.rationale: Normalize Gemini's literal 'null' string sentinel for specificJudge at extraction time (validateCausaServer), not with ad hoc guards at each call site.

nodes.label: EDR-007 (primary fix, referenced only)
nodes.rationale: Cited by application EDR-001 as the primary fix for judge/lawyer area binding; not present in this index's listed EDRs (001-006 application, 001-003 principles, 001 devops, 001 governance).

nodes.label: EDR-001: success_probability Interpretation
nodes.rationale: Judge prompts across modes interpreted success_probability inconsistently (author vs defense probability), producing wildly inconsistent results (5%, 50%, 85%) for the same case. Decision: success_probability always represents the AUTHOR's probability of winning (0-100), canonical in every mode; the display layer converts to the user's chosen side perspective. userSide/userPole/selectedMode must always be persisted together in Firestore to avoid partial-fallback side inversion on reload.

nodes.label: EDR-002: Commit Strategy
nodes.rationale: EAI? is a production system where bad commits directly affect paying users via auto-deploy; compound commits make debugging and rollback risky. Decision: atomic commits — one task per commit, always run git log --oneline -3 before starting, commit messages describe intent using type(scope): description, never bundle unrelated changes. AI agents must follow this and must not create compound commits.

nodes.label: EDR-003 (principles): Mode 4 Judge Frame Contract
nodes.rationale: A single bilateral judge frame caused 75-point run-to-run variance in Mode 4 when userSide==='DEFENSE', because static author petitions (claim-sympathetic language) vs AI-improved defenses (structured reasoning) let the judge model non-deterministically pick a claim-sympathetic or defense-quality interpretation frame. Decision: split the judge prompt by userSide — AUTHOR frame keeps the original stable bilateral 'who wins' framing; DEFENSE frame instead asks the judge to evaluate the technical soundness of the defense against the claim (same approach as Mode 2). success_probability still always represents the author's probability (EDR-001 invariant); the display layer inverts it for RÉU users. Frame is applied at inference/prompt time only, not at judge-agent creation time, preserving judge impartiality (EDR-003 application).

nodes.label: EAI? (Escritorio de Advocacia Inteligente) project
nodes.rationale: Legal simulation SaaS with five simulation modes. Stack: Vite 6 + React 19 + Express 4 + Firebase Auth + Firestore + Gemini 2.5 Flash + Stripe + Cloud Run. Production: eaijuridico.com.br (GCP gen-lang-client-0982741688). Staging: eai.radiokactus.com (GCP gen-lang-client-0783740660).

nodes.label: AGENTS.md: Mandatory XDRS Policy Consultation
nodes.rationale: All project decisions/working instructions must be captured as Policies or Skills in the XDRS structure. Before answering any request — including simple Q&A — the agent must read the XDRS root index, read relevant Policy files, and base actions on those Policies, with no exceptions. Must also verify work with build/test/lint, verify compliance with XDRS Policies, document new decisions as Policies when appropriate, and not perform git operations unless explicitly asked.

nodes.label: Modo 4 — correções aplicadas (13/06/2026)
nodes.rationale: Advogado melhora sobre petição anterior; analisa sentença do juiz; juiz sempre imparcial sem memória entre rodadas; isolamento por round; revisor de veredito (interpretJudgmentForSide) normaliza success_probability para perspectiva do autor antes de exibir; barra de força corrigida para DEFENSE; effectiveSide usa userSide ??
